sections.body: This field covers the ways artificial intelligence is now used in the daily work of researchers and teachers. It includes tools that search and summarize published studies, map citations, run statistical tests, code interview transcripts, draft grant sections, check manuscripts, build course materials, manage datasets, control lab instruments, and flag integrity problems. The work is practical, not theoretical, and it happens inside existing scholarly workflows. A researcher might use a literature review tool to find trials, a citation mapper to see who cites whom, or a writing assistant to shorten an abstract. The section describes what these tools actually do in each of those ten areas.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of this work is uneven. Some tasks, like finding papers and summarizing abstracts, are now routine and reasonably reliable. Others, like judging the quality of a study or catching subtle fraud, are not solved and often fail quietly. The honest limits are that these systems can miss relevant work, invent references, misread statistics, and reflect the biases of the papers they were trained on. The site's library holds 135 research papers and 11222 claims extracted from them, which is a small but real sample of the evidence, not a complete picture. No tool here replaces a careful human reader, and none should be treated as a source of truth on its own.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to find and combine studies should start with Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis, then use Citation Mapping and Discovery to see how those studies connect. For numbers, Quantitative Analysis and Reproducible Work covers statistical tools and scripts, while Qualitative Analysis and Mixed Methods covers interviews, text and coding. Grant Proposals and Funding and Academic Writing and Peer Review sit next to each other because they both deal with producing and judging written work. Course Design and Teaching moves from research into the classroom, and Research Data and Repositories covers where the underlying files live. Laboratory Automation and Simulation is the most hands on, dealing with instruments and experiments, and Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity is the frame around all the others, covering the rules that should guide every use.
